summary: PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication is healthy across node1, node2, and node3. node1 is writable; node2 and node3 are read-only streaming standbys. Replication uses TLS and peer-restricted 10.100.211.0/24 database addresses. All three nodes passed sequential OS-restart persistence tests.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled PostgreSQL 16.14 on all nodes.
Configured node1 as the writable primary with WAL streaming and dedicated physical slots for both standbys.
Created node-local private keys and CA-signed certificates for TLS certificate authentication.
Configured node2 and node3 as hot, read-only standbys with node-specific replication slots.
Bound PostgreSQL exclusively to each node's database IP and restricted port 5432 to database peers without a global firewall opening.
Committed probe data before and after the restart sequence, verified it on both standbys, and confirmed standby writes are rejected.
Restarted node2, node3, and node1 individually; verified changed boot IDs and full recovery before proceeding to the next node.

evidence.summary: Shows node-specific base backups and slots, two active streaming senders, caught-up replay LSNs, active physical slots, and TLS 1.3 certificate-authenticated sessions.

evidence.requirement: Writable primary and two read-only standbys replicate committed changes
evidence.summary: A post-restart transaction commits on node1; both standbys contain both committed rows, remain in recovery with transaction_read_only enabled, and reject real INSERT attempts.

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL traffic restricted to the dedicated database network
evidence.summary: Proves exact 10.100.211.10–12 listeners and replication endpoints, direct on-link routes, no globally opened 5432 port, peer-only firewall rules, certificate-only replication HBA entries, and established database-network sessions.
Shows CA-signed node certificates with correct SANs, verified certificate chains and key matches, and 0600 private-key permissions.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, automatic PostgreSQL recovery with intact data and streaming membership, then restored full two-standby health.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered read-only service/data/streaming membership, and full cluster catch-up.
Captures healthy writable-primary baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, persisted data, recovered exact listener, both TLS streaming members, active slots, and final caught-up state.
